messages.content: "Imagine you are a scientist working in a lab. You have a substance with a mass of 10 kilograms and a volume of 2 cubic meters. You want to calculate the density of this substance in kg/m³. After your experiment, you want to relax by doing some painting. You decide to mix two primary colors, red and blue. However, you want the resulting color to have a lightness level of 70%. Later, you have another substance with a mass of 5 kilograms and a volume of 1 cubic meter. You want to calculate the density of this substance as well, but this time in g/cm³. Finally, you decide to mix another set of primary colors, yellow and blue, but you want the resulting color to have a lightness level of 30%. Can you calculate the densities and mix the paint colors accordingly?"

function.name: calculate_density
function.description: Calculate the density of a substance based on its mass and volume. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kilograms.

volume.description: The volume of the substance in cubic meters.

unit.description: The unit of density. Default is kg/m³

function.name: mix_paint_color
function.description: Combine two primary paint colors and adjust the resulting color's lightness level. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

color1.description: The first primary color to be mixed.

color2.description: The second primary color to be mixed.

lightness.description: The desired lightness level of the resulting color in percentage. The default level is set to 50%.
